provider: misskey.gg — Misskey 2026.10, 1 TB drive per user

free_tier.stated: 1024000 MB = 1 TiB drive capacity PER USER. The per-object cap is 250 MiB: maxFileSizeMb reads 1024 (1 GiB) but the top-level maxFileSize of 262,144,000 bytes is the enforced field. This is the single largest per-user quota located on a live, registration-open fediverse instance.

per_object_cap.stated: 250 MiB per object, enforced by the top-level maxFileSize of 262,144,000 bytes
per_object_cap.notes: policies.maxFileSizeMb states 1024 (1 GiB) and the top-level maxFileSize states 262,144,000 bytes (250 MiB). The evidence entry notes that the top-level field is the cap actually enforced, so the record carries 250 MiB and the 1 GiB figure lives here as the field that lies.

egress.terms: Free. Media is served from a plain path on the instance domain (observed scheme: https://sss.<instance>/sss/<shard>/<uuid>) with `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable`. No egress meter, no bandwidth charge, no signed URL.

tooling: Misskey HTTP API is a clean JSON REST surface: POST /api/drive/files/create (multipart, `file` field) with an `i` (token) in the body; POST /api/drive/files/upload-from-url; POST /api/drive/files/delete; POST /api/drive/files (list). Token minted via MiAuth (GET https://<host>/miauth/<uuid>?name=...&permission=write:drive,read:drive) or POST /api/signin with username+password -> returns `i`, which is then just a query param. No library needed: it is a 20-line requests wrapper. rclone has no Misskey backend; write a thin one.
chaining: driveCapacityMb is a per-user soft counter enforced by the instance, not a hard technical wall — media attached to notes can still be served after the drive is full. Because each account is an independent counter and registration is open (API reports `disableRegistration: false`, `emailRequiredForSignup: true`), each account holds 1 TiB. Ten accounts hold 10 TiB. The provider accepts a single POST per account, so a client with mail control can register many.

limits.value: 250 MiB per object (top-level maxFileSize 262,144,000 bytes); policies.maxFileSizeMb claims 1 GiB and is not enforced
inviteLimit: 1` per 1440 min does NOT gate open signup

limits_note: per-object-cap 1 GiB (maxFileSizeMb=1024, verified 262144000 bytes = 250 MiB on most other instances, 524288000 = 500 MiB on misskey.io). Drive quota 1 TiB/user. Usage-anomaly controls: `inviteLimit: 1` per 1440 min does NOT gate open signup. Request-rate: Misskey applies a per-IP rate limiter on /api/drive/files/create (4096 req/hr default per IP, plus per-account limits, 250 MB/hr-ish effective on small instances).
reliability_note: Instance is a single volunteer-run host with ~small user count; a 1 TB drive is a published number, not a promise, and one operator decision or a disk-full incident takes everything offline at once. No SLA, no backup guarantee. Treat as 'high capacity, zero durability'.
confidence_note: The quota is a live API field read, not a page claim. The record stays documented because the identity field is inferred from prose, not read from the API. Was documented; now documented.

evidence.proved: driveCapacityMb = 1024000 (1,024,000 MB = 1 TiB per user); policies.maxFileSizeMb = 1024 while the top-level maxFileSize = 262,144,000 B = 250.0 MiB is the cap actually enforced; emailRequiredForSignup = true, disableRegistration = false. The per-object cap and the field's own location disagree, which is the trap.
